title: Rome's retort that the words mean only intercession: then why use the words of absolute prayer?
source_text: XCII. Regerunt, quum Sanctos eo modo precantur, mentem suam non esse, ut Sancti ea bona praestent & largiantur ipsi, propria quadam potestate, sed solum ut illa meritis & precibus suis a Deo obtineant. Adeoque licet verba aliud sonent, se tamen aliud non intelligere, quam ut Sancti intercessione sua quae petunt a Deo impetrent. Sed certe nihil eos cogit ut aliter sentiant, & aliter loquantur. Si non aliud rogant Sanctos quam ut Deum pro ipsis orent, cur utuntur apud ipsos verbis orationis absolutae; nec contenti sunt Sanctis ingeminare illud solenne, Ora pro nobis?
pass_a_gloss: They retort that, when they pray to the Saints in that way, their mind is not that the Saints themselves furnish and bestow those goods, by some power of their own, but only that they obtain them from God by their merits and prayers. And so although the words sound otherwise, they nevertheless understand nothing else than that the Saints obtain from God by their intercession what they ask. But certainly nothing compels them to think one thing and say another. If they ask nothing else of the Saints than that they pray to God for them, why do they use with them the words of absolute prayer; and are not content to repeat to the Saints that solemn Pray for us?
pass_b_english: They retort that when they pray to the saints in that way, they do not mean that the saints give and bestow those good things themselves by any power of their own, but only that the saints obtain them from God by their merits and prayers. So, although the words say something else, all they mean is that the saints obtain from God by intercession what is asked.

But surely nothing forces them to think one thing and say another. If they ask the saints only to pray to God for them, why do they address the saints in the words of absolute prayer? Why are they not content to repeat to the saints the familiar "Pray for us"?

lemmas.gloss: by some power of their own

choices.english: to think one thing and say another
rejected: to feel otherwise and speak otherwise
